item.title: Rotterdam night entry ban brings quiet, residents want it kept
item.description:
Rotterdam night entry ban brings quiet, residents want it kept

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Residents of the Rotterdam neighbourhood De Esch say the nights have been quiet since a ban on entering the area took effect two weeks ago, but fear the disruption will return when it runs out in October.

A curfew for anyone without a good reason for being in the area was imposed on July 23, making it an offence to be on the streets from 11pm till 5am. The unprecedented move follows years of persistent anti-social behaviour in the area, usually by people who don’t live there.

Police stopped about 100 people during the first fortnight, though no fines have been issued yet – the penalty is expected to be more than €100.

Quiet nights
“The windows can just stay open all the time,” one resident told broadcaster NOS. “It was very quiet from night one.”

Another resident told regional broadcaster Rijnmond that before the ban she had been kept awake almost every night by shouting and car horns, even with earplugs, and had slept well for the first time in a long while.

The neighbourhood, home to more than 4,000 people, had put up with street races, drug use and prostitution at night for years. Police research found that most of those responsible came from outside De Esch.

Police and the council say the disruption has not moved to other areas, but both note that it is the holiday season and the picture may change.

After October
The ban runs for three months and can be extended by another three after consultation.

The residents’ committee wants the neighbourhood closed at night once it ends, with marshals at the entrances at weekends letting in only people with a reason to be there.

The neighbourhood council, which advises the city, is against that. “It restricts the movement of other Rotterdammers too much,” its chairman Christiaan de Jong told NOS.

He said he hoped instead that behaviour would change and the disruption would be less than before. The council says it is too early to discuss a permanent solution, and that no other part of Rotterdam needs the same measure.

item.title: German zeppelin takes to Dutch skies to measure air pollution
item.description:
German zeppelin takes to Dutch skies to measure air pollution

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

People living in the Veluwe region near the German border have been surprised by the sight of a zeppelin hovering in the skies above their heads.

The airship took off from Essen, in the Ruhr area of North Rhine-Westphalia, and is being used to measure air pollution in an area on both sides of the border that covers Arnhem and Utrecht.

Scientists from Wageningen University & Research have equipped the balloon with instruments to measure levels of CO2 pollution, emissions and fine particles in the air, in a joint operation with German colleagues.

“The substances are partly produced by the forest and partly by traffic and industry,” researcher Michiel van der Molen told NOS. “Exactly how that works and how quickly it spreads is interesting, but mostly unknown.”

The zeppelin is due to pass over the area several times during the next week at a height of around 300 metres above ground level. Its path can be followed on Flightradar24 under the code DLZFN.

item.title: Thieves caught trying to retrieve cigarettes from police station
item.description:
Thieves caught trying to retrieve cigarettes from police station

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Thieves broke into a police station in The Hague to try to retrieve a batch of illegal cigarettes that were seized in a raid on Friday.

Four suspects were arrested when they were caught while trying to throw boxes of cigarettes over the fence of the police compound on Zichtenburglaan at 4.45am on Saturday.

One of the boxes caught on the fence and burst open, scattering cigarettes over the ground just as officers arrived on the scene.

The suspects tried to escape by car, but were forced off the road and arrested within 15 minutes later. One man was injured and taken to hospital under a police escort.

The haul of 1.2 million cigarettes was confiscated on Mandelastraat in Delft on Friday. Earlier in the week police recovered 500,000 iillegal cigarettes in two vans in the town.

Officers are investigating whether the break-in at the police station is linked to the earlier raids in Delft.

A12 motorway closed near The Hague after six-car collision

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The A12 motorway heading out of The Hague was briefly closed on Monday morning following a crash involving six cars.

The multiple pile-up happened near the Prins Clausplein junction at Nootdorp at around 10am. Police are investigating the cause.

Two ambulances were seen at the scene, but no details have been released about whether any drivers or passengers were injured.

Traffic in the Utrecht direction was diverted via the A20 and A13 via Rotterdam. One lane has since reopened.

item.title: Military intelligence chief exposed his home address on Strava
item.description:
Military intelligence chief exposed his home address on Strava

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The head of the Netherlands’ military intelligence service (MIVD) kept a public account on the fitness app Strava for years, allowing anyone to follow his cycling and running routes and work out where he lived, the Volkskrant reported on Friday.

Peter Reesink, a vice-admiral who has led the MIVD since February 2024, had logged activities that were visible to the public between 2018 and 2025. From the routes, the paper’s reporters could establish his home address, where he stored his camper, and when and where he went on holiday.

A public account breaches the defence ministry’s guidelines. Reesink made his account private immediately after the news got out, and has requested that it be deleted.

He told the paper he had not realised the account was still active, saying he had removed the app some time ago but forgot to delete the profile.

Own warning
The lapse comes at an awkward time; in the MIVD’s 2025 annual report, Reesink warned that Russia was becoming more aggressive and that large organisations were naïve about security. He told the Volkskrant at the time that people at his own briefings still asked whether they really needed to leave their phones outside.

It also comes days after the AIVD, the civilian intelligence service that works alongside the MIVD, was ranked third best in Europe in a survey of intelligence professionals.

The risks of these apps have been long established in the defence industry. In 2018, an investigation by De Correspondent and Bellingcat found that the fitness app Polar exposed the names and home addresses of thousands of military and intelligence staff worldwide, including a Dutch soldier deployed to Iraq.

item.title: Late Fortuna strike denies PSV opening-day win in Eredivisie
item.description:
Late Fortuna strike denies PSV opening-day win in Eredivisie

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Champions PSV Eindhoven were held to a draw in their opening Eredivisie match of the season as Fortuna Sittard hit a late equaliser in the Philips Stadion.

A mix-up between defenders Ryan Flamingo and Armando Obispo allowed Ole Romeny to sneak in and give Fortuna a first-half lead.

Flamingo made amends by heading in an equaliser early in the second half before Noah Fernandez put PSV in front in the 74th minute. But in injury time substitute Édouard Michut hit a fierce shot into the top corner to claim a point for the visitors.

Peter Bosz’s side were missing several key players, including new signing Kodai Sano, the injured Jerdy Schouten and the suspended duo Joey Veerman and Sergiño Dest.

“We’re not in top form, you saw that today,” the coach said afterwards. “In the first half especially we didn’t defend well.”

Derby win for Feyenoord

Feyenoord narrowly won the first Rotterdam derby of the season at Sparta in Giovanni van Bronkhorst’s first game since returning as manager, but only after the home side had two goals disallowed in injury time.

Milan Zonneveld was clearly offside on the first occasion, but the second decision was more contentious as the striker was penalised for nudging a defender just before he headed the ball past Tjark Ernst.

Luciano Valente scored the only goal in the 34th minute, drilling in a pullback from Gjivai Zechiël, who has returned to De Kuip after a loan spell at Utrecht.

Ajax laboured to a 2-0 win against PEC Zwolle, but only after the visitors had Sherel Floranus sent off early in the second half for a heavy tackle on Lucas Rosa.

Ajax had German duo Marc-André ter Stegen and Julian Brandt in the starting line-up, but not Belgian forward Mika Godts, who has been linked with a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

Godts, who said later he was suffering from a hamstring niggle, came on straight after the red card and laid on the second goal for Brandt in the closing minutes.

The breakthrough came from another Belgian substitute, Jordy Mokio, with the assist from new loan signing Tolu Arokodare.

Excelsior top table

Excelsior top the Eredivisie after the opening day after they kicked off the season with a thumping 4-0 win at newly promoted Cambuur Leeuwarden. Captain Noah Naujoks scored twice while Irakli Yegozian and David Garden, signed from amateur club Quick Boys, bagged the others.

Telstar’s Patrick Brouwer scored the fastest goal of the season, netting after just 27 seconds en route to a 2-1 win at NEC, who will need to regroup fast ahead of their Champions League second leg knock-out match against Olympiakos in midweek.

Twente also suffered a post-European hangover as they lost 1-0 at Heerenveen, Luca Oyen scoring with a near-post finish in the 52nd minute.

Goals from Brynjólfur Willumsson and Thom van Bergen earned Groningen a comfortable opening-day win against FC Utrecht, who replied with a late Adrian Blake strike in former Telstar coach Anthony Correia’s first match in charge.

Calvin Stengs marked his return to Alkmaar with the second goal in a 2-0 win for AZ against newcomers ADO Den Haag, while Go Ahead Eagles came back from 1-0 down to beat Willem II, the other promoted side, 4-1.

item.title: Heat returns as skies clear for Wednesday’s eclipse
item.description:
Heat returns as skies clear for Wednesday’s eclipse

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands is facing another hot, dry week, with temperatures climbing back above 30° from Wednesday and reaching 34 to 36° in the south by Thursday and Friday.

Monday and Tuesday will be cooler, staying under 30°, with some clouds and a chance of light rain in the north, but too little to ease the drought.

The clear spell is good news for the partial solar eclipse on Wednesday evening, when the moon will cover up to nearly 90% of the sun.

It will be visible across the country and begin around 7.15pm, ending just after 9pm. It will be the largest partial eclipse seen from the Netherlands since 1999. Anyone watching needs proper eye protection.

The returning warmth brings a strong chance of what would be the fifth regional heatwave of the year.

item.title: Demi Vollering wins final stage to seal Tour de Femmes title
item.description:
Demi Vollering wins final stage to seal Tour de Femmes title

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Demi Vollering claimed her second women’s Tour de France win with a stunning breakaway victory on the ninth and final stage to Nice.

Vollering attacked 600 metres from the summit of the final climb of the Col d’Èze to open up a 20-second lead on her only remaining challenger for the title, the Polish rider Katarzyna Niewiadoma.

It earned the 29-year-old from Pijnacker her third stage win in this year’s tour and confirmed her as the overall winner, 1 minute 18 seconds ahead of Niewiadoma.

The only other woman in contention going into the final day, the Swiss rider Marlen Reusser, crashed on the final descent and rolled in 24 minutes behind, finishing in 14th place overall.

Vollering hoisted her bike aloft after crossing the finish line alone for her first Tour de Femmes victory in three years, following second places in 2024 and 2025.

“I was thinking of a lot of things as I crossed the line,” she said. “My team, all the work that went into this, everyone who was behind me. I never doubted I could do this.”

Vollering started the day with an advantage of just eight seconds on Niewiadoma after claiming the yellow jersey with a similar breakaway in Saturday’s penultimate stage to Mont Ventoux.

On Sunday the riders had to tackle the Col d’Èze four times on a 99km circular route around Nice. Niewiadoma’s team-mate Zoe Bäckstedt set the early pace before Canadian Isabella Holmgren tested the leaders with a break on the third climb to the summit, but with 16km to go approaching the final summit, only Vollering and Niewiadoma were left out in front.

item.title: Rhine’s water flow drops to near 80-year low: shipping curbed
item.description:
Rhine’s water flow drops to near 80-year low: shipping curbed

August 10, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Rhine is carrying less water than at any point since 1947, leaving cargo barges unable to sail fully loaded, ferries and cruises cancelled, and watering restrictions for farmers.

The fact that this has happened in the height of summer, when the 1947 record was set in November, makes the situation far more serious, the national weather service KNMI has said, because much more water is being lost to heat and crop farming.

Over the past 24 hours the river carried an average of 614 cubic metres of water a second past Lobith in Gelderland, where it crosses from Germany, below the 620 recorded in 1947. Hydrologist Jan Verkade of the Deltares research institute and Rijkswaterstaat gave the figures to broadcaster NOS.

A warm spring melted the Alpine snow that goes into the Rhine about three months early, Verkade said, and the rain that usually follows has stayed away.

Ships, ferries and farms
The low water is already being felt across the country. Cargo barges cannot sail fully loaded, several locks have closed, and ferries and river cruises on the Rhine and its branches have been cancelled or cut short.

Farmers are facing bans on drawing water from ditches and streams for irrigation in some regions. Dozens of houseboats along the river have been left exposed on the riverbed, and are at risk of flooding when the water returns.

Drinking water is not affected, water authorities say, and regional water boards are sharing supplies around the country. The Netherlands remains at level two of a three-stage shortage scale – a shortage, but not yet a crisis.

The cabinet ruled out compensation last week for businesses hit by the drought, which the water minister estimated could run to tens or even hundreds of millions of euros in damage.

No rain in sight
Little rain is forecast for the coming days, and Verkade said the flow could fall below even the 575 cubic metres recorded in February 1929, when ice choked the current. The low water could last for weeks or months, he said.

The World Weather Attribution group of scientists found this summer that climate change had made the European drought far more likely, as warmer air pulls water from the soil and rivers faster.

Verkade said both extremes were sharpening: it is five years, almost to the season, since floods devastated parts of Limburg and the regions just over the German and Belgian borders.

item.title: Ajax, ING and Ace & Tate hit by data breach
item.description:
Ajax, ING and Ace & Tate hit by data breach

August 7, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Football club Ajax, bank ING and eyewear chain Ace & Tate have been caught up in the data breach at logistics firm CEVA Logistics, which came to light this week when Bol and De Bijenkorf warned customers their details may have been exposed.

CEVA handles deliveries for the companies and had access to the customer data needed to fulfil orders. The firm says it cannot rule out that personal details were leaked, although the companies affected say no payment details, usernames or passwords were taken.

Whether addresses, email addresses or phone numbers were exposed remains unclear.

At ING, the breach affects customers who ordered physical products through the bank’s rewards points scheme.

Ajax has advised supporters to be extra alert to phishing messages in the coming weeks. The club and Ace & Tate have both reported the breach to privacy watchdog AP, as Bol did earlier this week.

Ace & Tate has warned customers that current orders may be delayed, although online ordering is still running. CEVA said it would respond to the breach at a later stage.
